title: As you act, so you become
hookLine: Yajnavalkya tells King Janaka where karma begins: in what you want
carry: karma: as you act, so you become
tomorrow: where are you, in the part of the night you never remember?

cards: The alarm is set early. The running shoes wait by the door. Then morning comes, and the snooze button wins again.
Promises like that are easy to make at night. The Brihadaranyaka has a sentence about where change really starts, and it sits right beside today's great saying. Spoiler: not at the alarm clock.

teach.h: MADE OF ALL: DESIRE, ANGER, RIGHT, WRONG.
teach.b: The sage Yajnavalkya is teaching King Janaka, and one sentence of his keeps adding to its list.

In paraphrase: this self is Brahman, made of understanding, of mind, of breath, of sight and hearing, of earth and water, wind and space. Made of desire and not desire, anger and not anger, right and wrong. Made of all.
It's a bold move. The text doesn't tidy the self up first and only then call it Brahman. It names it Brahman while it's still full of wanting and anger.

teach.h: AS ONE ACTS, SO ONE BECOMES.
teach.b: As a person acts, as a person behaves, so that person becomes. The one who does good becomes good. The one who does harm becomes harmful.
This is one of the oldest statements of karma in Hindu scripture, and the verses go on to carry it into the next life too.
Read this way, karma isn't only a score kept from outside; it's the self being shaped by its own deeds. And the text adds what others say: a person is made of desire.
As the desire, so the resolve. In Sanskrit, the resolve is kratu, the settled will. As the resolve, so the deed.
And whatever deed is done, that is what one arrives at. So the chain doesn't start at the snooze button.
It starts further back, at what's wanted. The passage holds both in one breath: this self is Brahman, and this self is being shaped, choice by choice.

how: In Vedanta study, Brihadaranyaka 4.4.5 is read as a key passage on karma: what a person wants and resolves shapes what they do, and what they do shapes what they become.

o: this self is Brahman, even as deeds shape it
this world is made by Brahma, the creator
a pure self, once cleaned up, may become God

games.q: the self and the chain. tap the pairs.

s: in this passage, desire is simply bad and must be crushed
here desire is where the chain begins: as the desire, so the resolve, so the deed.
the passage says: as one acts, so one becomes
the one who does good becomes good; the one who does harm becomes harmful.

games.q: a friend says: 'i'm too angry and messy for any of this. you have to be pure before the self counts.' what does this passage do?
o: it calls the self Brahman while it's still made of desire and anger.
it says only a calm, pure self can ever be called Brahman.
it says anger proves the self isn't really there at all.
games.why: made of desire and not desire, anger and not anger, right and wrong: made of all. the text names it Brahman without tidying it up first.

practice: Many Hindus begin a puja or a vow with a sankalpa, a spoken resolve. Make a small one now. Name one thing you want to become this week, and one deed that would shape it.
Say it quietly, in a few words. If you pray, offer it to God, and let the breath come and go.

wordCard.voice: Ayam atma brahma: this self is Brahman, made of all things, and becoming what it does.

orig.note: Sanskrit: kratu, the resolve or settled will: as the desire, so the resolve.

carryVoice: Carry this: karma, as you act, so you become. As the desire, so the resolve, so the deed. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 4.4.5 (this self is Brahman, made of understanding, mind, breath, sight, hearing, earth, water, wind, space, fire and not fire, desire and not desire, anger and not anger, right and wrong, made of all; as one acts, so one becomes; a person is made of desire: as the desire, so the resolve; as the resolve, so the deed; what deed one does, that one attains)
